subject: humanities
passage: For centuries, makers of ajrak, a block-printed cloth closely associated with Sindh, in southern Pakistan, colored their work entirely with natural dyes, drawing deep red from madder root and blue from indigo, and a single piece could take two weeks or more to complete through repeated rounds of printing, dyeing, and washing. During the twentieth century, many workshops turned to synthetic dyes, which are cheaper, produce brighter colors, and shorten the process considerably. ______ a number of artisans have returned to natural dyes in recent decades, finding that some buyers will pay considerably more for cloth whose softer colors connect it to the craft's long history.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence lists the advantages of synthetic dyes: they are cheaper, brighter, and faster. The last sentence says some artisans have gone back to natural dyes anyway. A transition that signals something happening in spite of the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The advantages of synthetic dyes would not cause artisans to abandon them; the return to natural dyes happens despite those advantages.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Returning to natural dyes is not an example of workshops switching to synthetic dyes; it is the opposite movement.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" would mean the return to natural dyes resembles the switch to synthetic ones, but the two move in opposite directions.
explanation.D: Correct. "Even so" shows that some artisans returned to natural dyes in spite of the benefits of synthetic ones.
